snowpackStructure.comment:
The partly large amounts of new and wind-drifted snow in the westernmost Lower Valais, in the north and in large parts of Graubünden are in parts still prone to triggering. In the other regions, more recent wind slab accumulations are also in parts still prone to triggering, but usually smaller. In addition, avalanches can be triggered, above all on north and east-facing slopes, also in the upper layers of the underlying old snowpack.
With incoming radiation, numerous loose snow avalanches are to be expected from the new snow, especially in the main precipitation areas.
New and wind-drifted snow from the last few days is, above all on north-facing slopes in the high alpine regions, still in parts prone to triggering. At the transition to the underlying old snowpack, there are, above all on north and east-facing slopes at elevated altitudes, in parts still coarse-grained weak layers.

avalancheProblems.comment:
Weak layers in the old snowpack represent the main danger. Avalanches can be released by a single winter sport participant and reach large size in isolated cases. The avalanche prone locations are barely recognisable, even to the trained eye. Caution is to be exercised on little-used, rather lightly snow-covered shady slopes.
Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.
